name: Violent Reaction
label: Revelation
lede: Tom Pimlott was the only straight edge kid he knew in Liverpool, so he recorded Violent Reaction alone, moved to Leeds for a band, and ended up the first group from outside America that Revelation signed.

eras.title: The only straight edge kid in town
eras.text: Tom Pimlott lived in a northwest England city where, by his account, no one else was straight edge. He played every part himself and aimed for mean, not positive. He didn't expect anyone to listen.

years.big: "No one was Straight Edge" where he lived
q: I started this mainly because where I lived, no one was Straight Edge
years.src: DxR: Violent Reaction · Wikipedia: Violent Reaction
years.h: Pimlott records two demos alone, for a scene of one
years.p: Violent Reaction and Session One come out on Mind Rot Records, every part played by Tom Pimlott.
years.xp:
In a 2012 interview with DxR, Pimlott said he started Violent Reaction "mainly because where I lived, no one was Straight Edge." He wanted it to sound "mean, not like all those Straight Edge bands who are 'posi' or 'nice'."

He also said: "When I first started the band, I didn't expect anyone to listen to it, now there's people buyin records." The demos came out in 2011, and he played all the instruments himself until he built a live line-up.

years.cap: Violent Reaction at UK Edge Day, November 2012
years.src: Wikipedia: Violent Reaction · DxR: Violent Reaction
years.h: UK Edge Day 2012 puts a live band behind Pimlott
years.p: The self-titled Violent Reaction EP is out on Quality Control HQ, 6131 Records and Mind Rot, and Pimlott now has people on stage with him.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists three labels on the EP: Quality Control HQ, 6131 Records and Mind Rot. The DxR interview, posted in 2014, dates the move to Leeds as after UK Edge Day 2012.

In 2012 Pimlott said the plan was to record an LP the next year, but "we want to play show as much as we can."

eras.title: Leeds finds him a gang
eras.text: Moving to Leeds gave Pimlott a band, and the band gave Violent Reaction its sound: Negative Approach, Blitz, The 4-Skins and Straight Ahead, per Mass Movement. Then came two trips to America.

years.cap: Violent Reaction at Fluff Fest, Rokycany, Czech Republic, July 2013
years.h: Pimlott moves to Leeds and finds the rest of the band
years.p: Guitarists Tom "Razor" Hardwick and Charlie "Chubby Charles" Fresh, bassist Jimmy "J-Town" Wizard and drummer Nick "Skins" Sarnella join. Sarnella and Fresh also play in [[Arms Race|067526cd-2270-4e09-ade0-e0431b708de1]].

yt: Full set, Outbreak Festival, Leeds, Sept 14, 2013
years.p: The first full-length, made with the Leeds line-up and released by Painkiller Records. Mass Movement later described the sound as Oi-influenced straight edge hardcore streetpunk.

years.cap: Violent Reaction at Casal de Roquetes, Barcelona, July 14, 2013
years.h: First US tour, opening for Hounds of Hate
years.p: The Leeds band cross the Atlantic in support of [[Hounds of Hate|2a01d1e1-0a01-46b0-8a2c-2c839a6499c0]].

years.h: Callum Baird takes over bass from Jimmy Wizard
years.p: Wizard leaves Violent Reaction after about a year, and Baird plays bass from here to the end.

years.src: DxR: Violent Reaction · Wikipedia: Violent Reaction
years.h: The Flex open for them, and Pimlott drums in both bands
years.p: The Dead End EP comes out on Painkiller, and Violent Reaction headline a US tour with [[The Flex|1f7ba45c-19ca-48e8-b49d-eff0bfa1109d]]. Tom Pimlott plays drums for The Flex.
years.xp:
DxR says Pimlott met The Flex through the international band Sectarian Violence.

hate5six filmed a full Violent Reaction set on April 11, 2014, during this US run.

eras.title: Revelation looks abroad
eras.text: According to Wikipedia, Revelation had never signed a band from outside America before Violent Reaction. The group toured Marching On alongside sister band Arms Race and called it quits before 2017.

years.src: Wikipedia: Violent Reaction · Mass Movement: Revelation · Revelation Records
years.h: Marching On is Revelation's first record from a foreign band
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Violent Reaction are the first non-American band signed to Revelation. It comes out March 31, 2015, the day their spring US tour starts.
years.xp:
Mass Movement reported a worldwide deal with Revelation for the second album. It compared the sound to Negative Approach, Blitz, The 4-Skins, Straight Ahead, The Pist and 86 Mentality.

The lead single, 'Leave Me Out', premiered on Vice's Noisey. The record runs 14 tracks.

One wrinkle in the record: Mass Movement calls it the band's second LP, since City Streets came first in 2013.

years.h: Co-headlining the northeast with Arms Race
years.p: The tour opens March 31 at Cafe Saint Ex in Washington, D.C., with London's [[Arms Race|067526cd-2270-4e09-ade0-e0431b708de1]], a Violent Reaction spinoff.
years.xp: Mass Movement listed the dates: Washington D.C. (3/31), Philadelphia (4/01), Brooklyn (4/02), Boston (4/03), Rochester (4/05), Detroit (4/06), Chicago (4/07), Indianapolis (4/08) and Pittsburgh (4/09).

years.h: Violent Reaction announce the end in June, then tour Europe
years.p: Violent Reaction say they'll finish at the end of 2016, with a last European tour alongside Arms Race.
years.xp: The announcement came in June 2016, per Wikipedia. The last show on video is at DIYSF London on January 21, 2017, with Arms Race and The Flex on the bill.

eras.title: Behind the kit in Arms Race
eras.text: Tom Pimlott stayed in the family of bands his project had spun off.

years.h: Pimlott takes the drum stool in Arms Race
years.p: He plays [[Arms Race|067526cd-2270-4e09-ade0-e0431b708de1]] drums from 2016 to 2018, next to Violent Reaction's Nick Sarnella and Charlie Fresh. The band's last show is at Damage Is Done on November 22, 2019.
